Associations of variants in Analyses

Source: R/associations.R
og_associations.Rd

Returns the Associations of variants in analyses: for example, the outcome data for your instruments. Variants are rsIDs or ALIDs (see vignette("opengwasr")), mixed. The query runs as Jobs on the API, and og_associations() waits for them (see vignette("large-queries-and-jobs")).

Usage

og_associations(
  src,
  variants,
  analyses,
  observed_only = FALSE,
  original_units = FALSE,
  releases = NULL
)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api() or og_local().

variants

rsIDs and ALIDs, such as c("rs1421085", "16:53767042:C:T"). An ALID must be in canonical form (see og_alid()); anything else is an opengwasr_argument error.

analyses

Analysis identifiers (see og_analyses()).

observed_only

Leave out Imputed Associations (association_status == "imputed").

original_units

Give beta and se in the trait's original units, as in og_tophits().

releases

Store Releases to use, as in og_analyses().

Value

A data frame with og_provenance() attached.

Details

An rsID is resolved to every ALID it names in the Analyses' GWAS Stores (a multiallelic site names several), and you get every match; opengwasr never picks one. An rsID no GWAS Store holds has no Associations: you get a warning of class opengwasr_unresolved_variants, with the number as count and the rsIDs as ids. A variant an Analysis doesn't hold has no row. There is no LD-proxy option (ADR 0004): Reference-Completed Store Releases already hold an Imputed Association for most variants a source didn't report.

The columns are those of og_tophits(). Every row has an alid; its rsid is NA for a variant that has no rsID (the API sends ".").

One Job takes at most 1,000 distinct variants (ALIDs, after rsIDs are resolved), 100 Analyses and Analyses from 10 GWAS Stores. A larger request is split into several Jobs, run a few at a time (og_api(max_in_flight = )), and put back together: you get the rows an unsplit request would give, in a stable order (Analyses in the order asked; then chromosome 1-22, X, Y, MT and other contigs by name; then position; then ALID, whether one Job or several answered), with every Job in og_provenance(). A request the API refuses as too costly (opengwasr_request_too_large) is never split to get round that: see vignette("large-queries-and-jobs").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
og_associations(src, c("rs1421085", "16:53767042:C:T"), "OGS-00011:GCST003116")
} # }
